name: Myanmar
summary_text: Myanmar is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Section 377 of the Penal Code criminalises same-sex intimacy, and police use “shadow laws” — notably Section 30(d) of the Rangoon Police Act, allowing detention of anyone who cannot “satisfactorily account” for themselves — to target trans and gender-nonconforming people. Since the February 2021 coup the situation has turned lethal: the National Unity Government documented 17 LGBT people killed by mid-2022, and rights groups document arrests, torture, and sexual abuse of LGBT people by junta authorities, with the 2024 Conscription Law falling brutally on queer people. In 2025 the junta banned seven books for LGBTQ+ content as “obscene.” There is no legal gender recognition, no protection of any kind, and no institutional recourse — police and military are the primary predators. Resistance-controlled areas are nominally friendlier but are active war zones. For a visitor: any visible gender nonconformity risks detention under police-act powers, with torture documented in custody; the general security collapse compounds everything.

sources.title: Myanmar | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Section 377 criminalises same-sex intimacy, reinforced by 'shadow laws' and police discretion (e.g. Section 30(d) of the 1899 Rangoon Police Act used to detain people who cannot 'satisfactorily account' for their presence). Since the February 2021 coup, risks have intensified sharply - abuses in interrogation and detention reflecting homophobia, transphobia and punitive sexual violence; the UN Special Rapporteur warns of widespread sexual and gender-based violence against women, girls and LGBTQ people.

sources.title: LGBT discrimination on the rise since 2021 military coup- DVB
sources.claim_summary: DVB (Jan 2024): LGBT discrimination on the rise since the 2021 coup - attacks, arrest, torture and sexual abuse by authorities; the NUG Ministry of Human Rights stated 17 LGBT people were killed and two critically injured since Feb 2021; first-person accounts from trans women protesters.

Human Rights Myanmar submission (June 2024) to the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial executions: killing of LGBTIQ+ persons in military-controlled Myanmar - 5 to 12 individuals dead since the coup; Section 377 enforcement intensified as an aggravating factor; militarised policing, arbitrary detention and vague public-decency laws endanger the right to life.

sources.title: Myanmar junta bans 7 books with LGBTQ+ themes – Radio Free Asia
sources.claim_summary: RFA (Jan 2025): Myanmar's junta banned seven books with LGBTQ+ themes and will take legal action against their publishers, calling them 'obscene' and socially unacceptable - part of the community's long oppression in conservative Myanmar.

sources.title: The Silent Struggle: Myanmar’s LGBTQIA+ Community Under the Shadow of Conscription - The ASEAN SOGIE Caucus
sources.claim_summary: ASEAN SOGIE Caucus (March 2025): 'The Silent Struggle' - Myanmar's LGBTQIA+ community under the shadow of the 2024 Conscription Law, based on research by exile-led Queers of Burma Alternative; the law has forced queer individuals into a cycle of fear, discrimination and oppression, with legal frameworks stripping identity (forced into uniforms by assigned gender).

sources.title: Myanmar's transgender people not just chasing rainbows in fight for equality | Global development | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Feb 2016): 'Myanmar's transgender people not just chasing rainbows in fight for equality' - trans activists organising in Yangon despite colonial-era laws and police abuse.

sources.title: Gay man with HIV charged under Myanmar sodomy law
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Nov 2018): a gay man with HIV was charged under Myanmar's sodomy law (Section 377) - demonstrating active enforcement of the colonial-era criminalisation.

sources.title: Gay People In Myanmar Can't Live Openly. Here's Why | HuffPost The WorldPost
sources.claim_summary: HuffPost (Oct 2015): 'Gay People In Myanmar Can't Live Openly. Here's Why' - part of a 10-part series on LGBT rights in Southeast Asia; documents the 2013 Mandalay case where trans women were allegedly forced to strip in public by police; notes nat kadaws (spirit mediums) as trans women or transvestite men within Burmese culture.
